The company trades at a P/E ratio of 6.54x, significantly lower than its sector benchmark of 18.55x [E6], indicating that investors may not fully recognize the value they are purchasing. Additionally, DOLATALGO's Price-to-Book (P/B) ratio is just 0.92x [E2], suggesting that the stock could be undervalued relative to its book value. Despite these positive indicators, the company has underperformed in terms of compounded profit growth over both five and three years [-3% and 4%, respectively] [E17, E18]. However, DOLATALGO's strong sales growth of +68% YoY [E62, E63] and profit growth exceeding 20% YoY [E65, E71] are notable improvements that have outpaced expectations. Furthermore, the company's recent compounded profit growth exceeds one-year price growth by 57%, indicating a strong performance relative to market expectations [E54]. While these factors suggest potential value, they do not outweigh the negative aspects of its underperformance in profit growth over five years and its operating margin decline from 66% three years earlier to 59% TTM [-7 percentage points] [E27]. Despite these challenges, DOLATALGO's strong sales growth and positive profit momentum provide compelling evidence that it is being undervalued by the market.
